# `selora completion [bash|zsh|fish]`

Prints a shell completion script to stdout. The script is **generated from the
live commander program** at run time — command names, descriptions, and every
option (including the globals) are walked from the same program object that
parses your commands — so it cannot drift from what `selora --help` shows.

```
$ selora completion bash | head -4
# selora bash completion — generated by `selora completion bash`.
# Load it in the current shell:  eval "$(selora completion bash)"

_selora_commands="login logout whoami balance usage models model keys chat init run completion"
```

## What it completes

- **Commands** — every registered subcommand, with the description shown by
  `selora --help` where the shell supports it.
- **Flags** — every option of the current command plus the global
  `--debug`, `--json`, `--api-url`, and `-h/--help`/`-V/--version` at the root.
- **`keys` sub-actions** — `list`, `create`, `revoke` (the one command whose
  first argument is a fixed vocabulary).
- Nothing after a value-taking option (`--api-url`, `--key`, `--model`,
  `--name`): the CLI cannot know valid values, so it offers none — never a
  guess.

It does **not** complete model ids, key ids, or URLs: the scripts are static
and make no network calls.

## Installing

| Shell | One-off                            | Persistent                                                                                                     |
| ----- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| bash  | `eval "$(selora completion bash)"` | add the same line to `~/.bashrc`                                                                               |
| zsh   | `source <(selora completion zsh)`  | `selora completion zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_selora` (a directory on your `fpath`), or source it from `.zshrc` |
| fish  | —                                  | `selora completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/selora.fish`                                              |

## Defaulting from `$SHELL`

`selora completion` (no argument) picks the shell from the basename of
`$SHELL` when it is `bash`, `zsh`, or `fish`. When `$SHELL` is unset or
something else, it prints usage with the three shells and exits 1 — it never
guesses a shell that was not asked for.

```
✗ Usage: selora completion <bash|zsh|fish>
· Prints a completion script for the given shell to stdout.
· bash:  eval "$(selora completion bash)"
· zsh:   source it from .zshrc, or drop it on your fpath as _selora
· fish:  selora completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/selora.fish
```

An unknown argument is an honest error (`Unknown shell: powershell — expected
bash, zsh, or fish.`), exit 1.

## Flags

Global: `--debug`, `--json`, `--api-url <url>` (they have no effect on the
generated script — the script content depends only on the program itself).

## `--json`

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "shell": "bash",
  "script": "# selora bash completion — generated by ...\\n..."
}
```

The script as a single JSON string field — useful for tooling that installs
completions programmatically.
